phases.title: Roadmap Maintenance, Console Tooling and Follow-up Insertion

runs.title: Audit and correct the roadmap content objective by objective
runs.summary: Human-led assessment of every objective, phase and run in roadmap.json, correcting each objective in place before moving to the next.
runs.full_description: This run is an audit: the artifact already exists, so the work is judgement rather than implementation. The execution stage is the operator's own assessment, walking the roadmap one objective at a time and judging each run against reality: whether its status reflects what actually happened, whether its description still matches the work, and whether it is duplicated, superseded, missing or misplaced. Alongside the operator's own feedback, each objective is also checked for current naming (Cantu Studio, Editor, Web Engine, Slides Engine, Project Console) and for retired certification vocabulary, preserving scope disclaimers as live guardrails while cleaning certification disclaimers as residue: where old text states something true in a dead language, the fact is preserved and the word is changed. AI assists by mapping and presenting the current content and by reviewing the corrections for consistency, but the verdict is the operator's. Findings whose verdict is already known are corrected in place within this run, through the roadmap tool rather than by hand-editing the file. A finding that needs a verdict this run cannot give, or work that does not fit an in-place content correction, becomes its own follow-up run at the moment it appears. An objective is corrected and approved by the operator before the next objective is opened. This run closes when every objective has been assessed and approved.

runs.title: Build the roadmap maintenance and follow-up insertion tool
runs.summary: Design and implement a command-line tool that inserts, moves, removes and edits roadmap runs while keeping queue_order contiguous, dependencies valid and run identity stable.
runs.full_description: Editing roadmap.json by hand is the main cost of maintaining the roadmap: every insertion resequences the whole tail, every move risks inverting a dependency, and a single off-by-one fails the validator. This run designs and builds a bounded command-line tool that performs those edits safely. It must support inserting a run before or after an existing run and at the end of a phase, moving a run to a new position, removing a run, swapping two runs, and editing a run's text fields and dependencies. After every operation it must automatically resequence queue_order so it stays unique and contiguous from one, verify that each dependency still precedes its dependents with no cycles, refuse any edit that would orphan a depends_on reference, preserve every existing run_id as a stable identity, preserve the file's byte-level encoding including its em-dashes, and run the Project Console validator as a self-check, refusing to write when the validator would fail. It writes only to the roadmap source and performs no Git action. The tool is a command-line surface: it does not add write actions to the Project Console, which stays read-only. Making the console itself editable is a separate decision that would build on this tool's core logic rather than replace it.

runs.title: Make the Project Console edit the roadmap
runs.summary: Add roadmap editing to the Project Console, reusing the command-line tool's core so the console can insert, move, remove and edit runs, phases and objectives with the same safety guarantees.
runs.full_description: The Project Console was built read-only on purpose: it renders project state and does not mutate it. This run revisits that decision for roadmap content specifically, because auditing and maintaining the roadmap through the command line is slower than doing it where the roadmap is already displayed. It adds a write path for roadmap edits only: the console gains an editing surface for runs, phases and objectives, backed by a server endpoint that imports the existing roadmap core module rather than reimplementing its logic, so every edit keeps the same guarantees - queue_order stays contiguous, dependencies still precede their dependents, no cycles, no orphaned dependencies, identity is never mutated, and the file is written atomically with the validator as the authority. The console keeps rendering everything else read-only; this run does not turn it into a control plane for the project, does not schedule work, and does not mutate any state other than the roadmap source. It supersedes the read-only boundary only for roadmap content, and the objective and foundation text that assert a fully read-only console must be updated to say so.

runs.title: Add dev launchers for the Project Console and the Editor
runs.summary: Add tools/dev launchers so the Project Console and the Editor are started the one supported way.
runs.full_description: The Project Console was being started with an ad-hoc static one-liner on port 8765 that does not implement POST /__project-console/roadmap/edit or the History sync route, so edit mode correctly refused to turn on and sync returned 404. This run adds tools/dev with two double-clickable launchers and a shared helper library: start-project-console (node serve-project-console.mjs on 8787) and start-editor (npm --prefix tools/author-lite run dev, which starts compiler-api on 3000 and editor-ui on 5173). Repo root is derived from each launcher's own location and then verified; nothing is hardcoded to a machine. The Editor launcher resolves the lessons workspace to the JAME_Lessons sibling repo one level up, honors AUTHOR_LITE_WORKSPACE_ROOT when already set, and exits without creating anything when the workspace is missing. Committed as af45907. This run claims no Human QA of the console editor itself.

runs.title: Make the roadmap editor usable for the content audit
runs.summary: Correct the console roadmap editor after Human QA: start-up guidance, insert position, dependency picker, objective reorder and archive, batched edits, and title-only objectives and phases.
runs.full_description: Human QA of the console roadmap editor drove a series of usability corrections. The snapshot-load banner told the operator to serve the repo with a plain static host, which lacks the edit and history-sync endpoints; it now names serve-project-console.mjs on 8787. The insert form gained an editable Position field prefilled from the anchor, so the resulting queue_order is visible before preview instead of after. The dependency picker dropped its 30-item truncation and its search box in favour of a dropdown of every eligible run, scoped to runs earlier than the chosen position. Objectives gained presentational reordering and a manual archive flag, with a collapsible Archive section at the bottom of the tree; the core refuses archiving an objective that holds an active run. Per-block preview buttons were replaced by one global Preview all changes that batches every changed field into a single dry-run, confirm and write. Objectives and phases were reduced to a title only; summary and full_description were removed from the schema, the data and the console, and remain recoverable from Git. A latent defect was found and fixed along the way: phase and objective text editing never reached the core because the payload sent the wrong target keys. Commits f5e2dcc, e4fc911, ec90db6, 0a9bb58 and 367d3ec.

runs.title: Make it possible to close an active run
runs.summary: Design and implement the missing route from active to completed without weakening the progress invariant or fabricating progress.
runs.full_description: There is no route from active to completed. A completed run requires every progress entry to be in state done; the console does not edit progress by design, because progress is an execution record and editing it rewrites history; and set-status refuses transitions that would need fabricated progress. The result is that RUN-CANTU-ROADMAP-CONTENT-AUDIT-001 cannot be closed at all once its assessment is finished. This run designs and implements the missing route. It must not weaken the core invariant: a completed run still may not hold a non-done progress entry, and nothing may be fabricated. Note that progress is optional in the model: a run may go planned to active to completed with no progress array, which is how the tooling runs closed. AIW is not connected, so the progress cycle is currently cost without benefit; the operator may prefer runs that carry no progress until AIW returns.

runs.title: Fix three latent console defects found during editor QA
runs.summary: Correct the Overview active-run label fallback, the missing model-cache fallback in the edit modal, and the Add run position default that asserts a false execution order.
runs.full_description: Three latent defects surfaced during operator Human QA of the console editor, none of them blocking today. First, the Overview's active-run label falls back to the literal Now when no run is active, so once the audit run closes a planned run will be labelled as work in progress; this appeared when the queue readiness groups merged. Second, v3EditBeforeNode reads roadmapV3ModelCache without the fallback that v3OpenEditModal has, so if the cache were empty with the modal open the Position field would render but Preview all changes would report no changes. Third, the Add run affordance defaults to end-of-phase, which in an early phase produces a low queue_order that asserts the run executed near the start of the project; the launchers run nearly landed at position 2 this way.

runs.title: Add phase and objective create and delete operations
runs.summary: Add the phase and objective create and delete operations the roadmap tool lacks, so structural corrections like new phases and removed objectives do not need hand-editing.
runs.full_description: The roadmap tool implements all run-level operations, including run insert, move, remove and swap, but it has no operation to create or delete a phase or an objective. Consequences: the Project Console objective has no phase for meta-work, because its three phases predate the decision that system and console work opens a run, so the dev launchers landed in Roadmap Maintenance for want of a better home; the two ghost phases left over from the Web component regrouping cannot be deleted; and any structural correction the audit finds at the phase or objective level needs hand-editing roadmap.json, which is what the tool exists to avoid. This run adds phase and objective create and delete through the core, the shared plan, the CLI and the console, following the same pattern by which objective move and archive were added. The single unavoidable core change is extending the identity guard to accept a sanctioned added or removed phase or objective id, since it currently rejects any change to those id sets. Deletion needs a design decision the operator has not made: refuse when the phase or objective still holds children, or cascade. The existing precedent is refusal with an explicit opt-in flag, as run removal already refuses when dependents exist.

runs.title: Deep Project Console audit
runs.summary: Full human-led audit of the Project Console surface, deferred until Cantu Studio development is further along.
runs.full_description: A thorough audit and classification of the whole Project Console surface, deferred deliberately. The operator decided that auditing the console in depth now would stall product development, and that the console is good enough at a coarse level for the work it currently serves. This run stays planned until Cantu Studio is further developed and the console has accumulated real operational use. It has no dependencies and is not gated by anything; it is a horizon item the operator pulls forward when the time is right. It is distinct from the bounded defect work already queued: the latent console defects run corrects three known defects found during editor QA, while this run looks for what nobody has looked for yet.

runs.summary: Read-only map of what the console does today vs what the master console needs, and of the three couplings that tie it to Cantu.
runs.full_description: Read-only. What the console does today vs what the master one needs, and the three couplings that tie it to Cantu: validator anchors over the console source, edit endpoint (Cantu-local tooling), RUN-JAME- regex of the history builder. What comes out is a MAP, not code. Executed and adjudicated: the map lives at context/aiw-console/records/AUDIT-CONSOLE-O4-PHASE0.md (commit dc76b49). Objective framing, preserved literal from RM-AIW:114-120 and therefore left in the language of its source (no home at objective level under roadmap_tree_v1): SECUENCIA ACORDADA (D-034) — la consola es lo SIGUIENTE y va primero. Razón: no es solo que dé orden de trabajo, es que la consola es la CONDICIÓN que hace seguro el modelo de 3 conversaciones en paralelo (sin ella, cada conversación lee packs pegados a mano y las verdades divergen). Definición de "consola estable" = renderiza los tres proyectos, leyendo de sus propios repos, roadmap + docs + status, READ-ONLY. Nada más; edición y UX vienen después y ya pueden ir en paralelo.

runs.title: aiw-console emits its own .project/ folder
runs.summary: The projector starts emitting aiw-console's .project/ folder according to the contract (schemas, names, freshness).
runs.full_description: aiw-console emits its own .project/ folder via the projector (tools/projector/project.mjs), materializing the contract: family v1, .project/ replaces views/ (contract §1.b), generated_at required and the new key sources with mtime to make the rot detectable (contract §6). The path obstacle is still single and localized: resolveInsideAiw (tools/projector/project.mjs:475-483) THROWS if the destination leaves .aiw/ (D-043). SCOPE REDEFINED BY D-048, with the source measurement in front of it (records/MEDICION-FUENTES-CONSOLA.md). FUNCTIONAL MINIMUM — what it takes for the identical console to light up with its five tabs, measured with the renderer in hand: (1) views/project_console.snapshot.json, the required GATE without which the whole console falls back; (2) the roadmap of its own, which feeds Overview + Roadmap + Queue; (3) views/git_history.snapshot.json, which is already emitted on its own. Those three have an origin and an emitter today. Plus the THREE sources that do not exist today and do paint live pixels: docs/docs_index.json (the entire Docs tab), guardrails/project_guardrails.json and guardrails/no_claims.json (the two data tables of Governance State). That is the minimum: the snapshot as the gate, the three emittable ones, and the three to be created. DEFERRED — the other NINE of the twelve without an emitter buy no live pixel: project.json, state/project_status.json, state/component_status.json, state/events.jsonl, ledgers/change_ledger.jsonl, ledgers/git_provenance.jsonl, ledgers/human_qa.jsonl, ledgers/ai_reviews.jsonl and guardrails/project_memory.jsonl. They only silence the aggregate banner of optional sources and fill two Console Diagnostics counts (component_status and git_provenance); the rest feed dormant code only, and project_memory.jsonl does not have a single consumer in the renderer. They are DEFERRED to a later and OPTIONAL COSMETIC PARITY phase that D-048 does NOT open: it will be opened only if the operator asks for it, and each source comes in through the contract's normal door (§18.b) the day it has an emitter. They are parity-with-Cantu debt, not functional-console debt. TWO NEW PIECES OF WORK THAT THE MEASUREMENT UNCOVERED and that this run did not contemplate: (a) THE PROJECTOR CANNOT PROJECT AIW-CONSOLE TODAY — it reads the objectives/{pending,parked,processed}/*.md, logs/<id>/summary.md and config.json layout of a project root, and aiw-console HAS none of the three; it has to be taught to project aiw-console taking its own roadmap/roadmap.json (roadmap_tree_v1) as the ROOT of the tree and package.json as minimal identity. A reminder whose cost has already been paid once: the .aiw/ of aiw-console is NOT state of its own, it is the delivery area of AIW's projection (D-044), so the origin is not read from there. (b) docs_index.json HAS TO BE CREATED FROM SCRATCH — it does not exist at any path in the repo (glob of the whole repo = 0 hits), but the corpus DOES exist: 23 real .md. It is the only 'cuerpos sin índice' (bodies without an index) case, and creating the index IS creating the source: shape with docs[] and, per entry, title/path/nav_tier/default_visible/audience/freshness; curation of what is shown by default; and paths that exist on disk, which is what the validator demands. Inherited pending item that moves with this run: the rename of jame.git_history_snapshot.v1 (contract §19) drags along the render gate that compares that literal — emitter and new console move together in that chain; and the commit↔run association degrades because of the RUN-JAME- regex (audit E.1). ONE run until the stage is planned in detail. DELIVERED AND CLOSED (record closeout, 2026-07-25). Evidence: `context/aiw-console/records/EMISOR-CARPETA-PROPIA-O4-P2.md`, and on disk the `roadmap_tree` root mode in `tools/projector/project.mjs` —decided by the SHAPE of the root, never by its name—, the declared sources `governance/{guardrails,no_claims,contract}.json` that were born here, and the files under `.project/`. The decision this run took and that was never recorded —the envelope transports the vocabulary per axis and the derivation precedence as an executable table; the RESULT does not travel— was written down as D-049, six pieces after being applied in code.

runs.title: Identical port of Cantu's console onto aiw-console's sources
runs.summary: Transplant Cantu's console as it is (index.html + project-console.css + the real renderer) into aiw-console, with the data layer pointed at its own sources and with no JAME identity. A single project: the multi-console comes later.
runs.full_description: IDENTICAL MIGRATION, asked for by the operator and adjudicated in D-048: before the multi-console, Cantu's console is transplanted into aiw-console as it is, for a single project. It is not a redesign nor a prototype — it is a PORT, and the done criterion is the resemblance. WHAT IS TRANSPLANTED: the three real pieces of projects/cantu-studio/docs/project-console/ — index.html with its FIVE tabs (Overview; Roadmap with its two subviews, Run Queue and Roadmap; History; Docs; Status with Governance State and Console Diagnostics — there are no separate 'Queue' or 'Governance' tabs), assets/project-console.css, and assets/project-console.js, THE REAL RENDERER, not a rewrite from scratch. WHAT IT IS POINTED AT: the data layer stops reading ../../.aiw/** —which in this repo is the delivery area of AIW's projection, not state of its own (D-044)— and starts reading the sources the previous run emits. Mechanics already measured: of the 15 paths of the PATHS table only the snapshot is required; the other 14 go fail-soft, so a tab without a source is born empty instead of breaking the console. Which ones are born empty is measured beforehand (records/MEDICION-FUENTES-CONSOLA.md §F.3) and does NOT count as a defect of the port. WHAT IDENTITY IS REMOVED, at the points already located by the audit (records/AUDIT-CONSOLE-O4-PHASE0.md, Block E): the RUN-JAME- regex of the history-builder (E.1) and the strip regex of the renderer; the baked-in run constants and the RUN_OPERATOR_OVERRIDES map keyed by twelve run_id of Cantu (E.2), which simply match nothing here; the baked-in .aiw/ paths (E.3); and the branch fallback string jame-parallel-audit-001 (E.4). Watch out for the coupled pair: the render gate that demands the literal jame.git_history_snapshot.v1 moves together with the rename of the emitter, neither before nor after. GATE (real depends_on): it depends on RUN-CONSOLE-EMISOR-CARPETA-PROPIA-001 — with no own sources emitted there is nothing to render, and with the snapshot absent the whole console falls back. BOUNDARY: a single project on purpose. The side menu and the multi-project screen are the NEXT run, not this one. ONE run until it is planned in detail. DELIVERED AND CLOSED (record closeout, 2026-07-25). Evidence: `context/aiw-console/records/PORT-IDENTICO-CONSOLA-O4-P11.md`, and on disk `project-console/` with `index.html`, `assets/project-console.{css,js}` and `serve.mjs`. The three pieces travelled byte for byte from `cantu-studio/docs/project-console/` and the work was done on the copy: the CSS without a single rule changed, the HTML with one line (the `<title>`). Its FINISHING —Docs and the `git_history` emitter— is the next run of this same phase, and until this closeout it had no run.

DELIVERED AND CLOSED — evidence in `context/aiw-console/records/ACABADO-DOCS-Y-EMISOR-GIT-HISTORY.md`. What it did, in three pieces: (a) DOCS — four elements were removed from the transplanted renderer, all invisible in Cantu and all dead here (the *By category* / *By retention class* toggle, its explanatory note, the `retention_class` label that said `UNCLASSIFIED` in 27 of 27 rows, and the tier label); (b) the *Edit roadmap* button was left `hidden`, NOT DELETED — the element with its `id`, the call site, the probe of the endpoint, the text of the refusal and the whole edit modal are kept intact, so restoring it the day a write path exists is deleting one attribute (Block C); (c) THE EMITTER of `.project/git_history.json`, written in `tools/projector/project.mjs` and not in the old history-builder, which was not touched — one folder, one emitter, one guard; `PROJECTOR_VERSION` goes up 0.3.0→0.4.0 because an emitter that writes six files is not the one that wrote five. The run↔commit association comes out of the project's own roadmap and no `run_id` prefix is left baked in; measured: 0 of 35 commits name a `run_id`, and the column is left blank instead of being filled. runs.title: The curated docs index is TRANSPORTED; the scan stays as a fallback
runs.summary: Adjustment on `O4.P4`: a project that already curated its docs index receives that index republished, not a dump of all its `.md`.
runs.full_description: Adjustment on `O4.P4` (`RUN-CONSOLE-CANTU-EMITE-CARPETA-001`), delivered the same day. Run CREATED IN THE RECORD CLOSEOUT of 2026-07-25 to cover a record that was orphaned; it adopts the `run_id` that the record itself already declared in its header, so that the citation of the record becomes true without editing it. DELIVERED AND CLOSED — evidence in `context/aiw-console/records/DOCS-INDICE-CURADO-TRANSPORTADO.md`, RENAMED in that same closeout: it carried `-O4-P5` and thereby claimed a phase that was not its own (`O4.P5` is parity, operator QA), when the work was an adjustment to `O4.P4`. The defect it corrects: `O4.P4` emitted for Cantu a `docs_index` by SCANNING all the `.md` of its repo. It was the only behaviour the emitter had, and for the project that inaugurated it it was the right one —this repo had no index and its own was built from scratch in `O4.P2`—; applied to a project that DID curate its own, the same scan silently replaces a curation with a dump. The rule stands: if the `docs_index` path of the layout brings a conforming index, it is TRANSPORTED with its selection and its order verbatim; if not, it is SCANNED, and the scan survives as a fallback. It is decided by the PRESENCE of the file at that path, never by the name of the project: a root that grows a curated index tomorrow starts being transported on its next emission without a line of code being touched. Test: `tests/projector-docs-transport.test.mjs`.

phases.title: Write — the console edits the roadmap (dry-run→confirm) and syncs the history

runs.title: The two write paths the global console does not have
runs.summary: Roadmap editing from the UI with a dry-run→confirm flow, and history sync. Phase opened by D-050; this commission records it and places it, it does not design it.
runs.full_description: NEW phase opened by D-050, which reverses the deferral that D-034 had fixed: there 'consola estable' (stable console) was defined narrowly as READ-ONLY, with editing and UX explicitly afterwards. The reason for the change, recorded: the global console CANNOT REPLACE Cantu's if it cannot do what Cantu's does, and the cutover (`O4.P7`) is irreversible. The operator asked for it after the visual QA, and AUDIT Block F.3 had already foreseen exactly this loss. SCOPE, fixed here and only this: the TWO missing write paths. (1) ROADMAP EDITING from the UI with a dry-run (`apply:false`) → confirm (`apply:true`) flow, which is the flow already measured in Cantu's console (AUDIT F.3: the endpoint `/__project-console/roadmap/edit` in its server, with `handleRoadmapEdit`, which 'writes nothing but the canonical roadmap.json'). (2) HISTORY SYNC, the endpoint that regenerates the git history, absent today by construction: `project-console/serve.mjs` declares it in its header —'no roadmap edit endpoint, no history sync endpoint, no snapshot rebuild, no Git command, no watcher'—. THIS RUN DESIGNS NOTHING: the commission that opened the phase recorded it and placed it; the design is its own work the day it is planned in detail. ONE run until then. TWO MEASURED FACTS IT WILL HAVE TO RESOLVE, verified on disk on 2026-07-25: (a) THE EDIT ENGINE IS NOT IN THIS REPO — `roadmap-core.mjs`, `roadmap-plan.mjs` and `roadmap-edit.mjs` exist ONLY in `cantu-studio/tools/roadmap/`, and `aiw-console/tools/roadmap/` DOES NOT EXIST; in Cantu the endpoint of the server and the CLI share the SAME orchestration `roadmap-plan.mjs` over `roadmap-core.mjs`, so what is missing here is the whole engine, not an endpoint on top of an engine that is present. (b) THE PATH OF THE CANONICAL ROADMAP DIFFERS PER PROJECT — in aiw-console it is `roadmap/roadmap.json`; in cantu-studio it is `.aiw/roadmap/roadmap.json`. A multi-project writer cannot bake in a path: it resolves it per project, as the emitter already resolves the layout by the SHAPE of the root. And the corollary that neither of the two lets you negotiate: `.project/` is DERIVED (§1.b, §2, §18) and IS NOT A WRITE DESTINATION — the canonical one is written and re-emitted; writing into `.project/` would be editing the copy that rots, which is the failure mode the whole contract exists against. DOOR ALREADY PREPARED, and it is work that does not have to be redone: the *Edit roadmap* button was left `hidden` and not deleted, with the element, the call site, the probe of the endpoint and the edit modal whole (`records/ACABADO-DOCS-Y-EMISOR-GIT-HISTORY.md`, Block C) — restoring it is deleting one attribute. PLACEMENT: what comes NEXT after the record closeout of 2026-07-25, before `O4.P5` (parity), `O4.P6` (AIW as third project) and `O4.P7` (cutover). The order is carried by the position in the array and by `queue_order`, not by the number: `phase_id` is opaque identity and `O4.P12` is the next free id, not a position (D-047).

runs.title: `start-console` launcher at the root of the repo
runs.summary: Double-click startup for the multi-project console: it verifies the checkout, frees the port, opens the browser. Tooling, not a console stage.
runs.full_description: TOOLING work, not console-stage work: that is why it lives in the cross-cutting phase and not in the sequence of stages. Run CREATED IN THE RECORD CLOSEOUT of 2026-07-25 — the work was delivered with no run to cover it. DELIVERED AND CLOSED. IT HAS NO RECORD OF ITS OWN, and none was invented for it: its documentation is `start-console.README.md`, and the files are `start-console.cmd` and `start-console.ps1` at the root of the repo. What it does, according to that documentation: it derives the root of the repo from the location of the launcher itself and VERIFIES it by demanding `project-console/serve.mjs` and `project-console/projects.json` —no absolute path, no machine or user name baked in, so it works in any checkout and from any directory—; it stops the node process holding the port and verifies that it was freed, which is the failure it exists for (an old server holding the port and serving earlier code while one believes one is looking at the current one), and if whoever holds it is NOT node it reports so and refuses to start instead of fighting for it; it prints the exact URL and opens the browser when the port responds. Port 8788 by default —that of the server itself—, `PC_PORT` replaces it and the launcher operates on that one: it is the one it frees, verifies, prints and opens. What it starts is READ-ONLY: starting the console cannot change this repo nor any of the ones it reads. `depends_on` declared over the shell and not empty because `project-console/projects.json` —one of the two files the launcher demands in order to start— was born in `O4.P3`.

NO mockups and no invented data — that is exactly the pattern of the hand-written v0.3 that the contract exists to kill (D-039). It is besides the FIRST REAL CONSUMER of roadmap_tree_v1 (layer 2 of the contract, D-040), so it exercises the consumer-test doctrine (D-026) BEFORE the emitter is built: if the format does not hold up, it is known here and not three phases later. New phase O4.P10, placed THIRD in the objective (after the contract O4.P1, before the emitter O4.P2), to give a visible result early. It is the FIRST GATE of operator approval: RUN-CONSOLE-SHELL-MULTIPROYECTO-001 depends on this prototype being APPROVED and is not built in parallel. The gate requires explicit operator approval. ONE run until it is planned in detail. RETIRED AS A PHASE DELIVERABLE BY D-048 — the operator asked for an IDENTICAL MIGRATION of Cantu's console before the multi-console, with which the order that this run inaugurated (D-047: the prototype first) is reversed. NOTHING IS DELETED: the console/ prototype is still on disk and its knowledge deliverable is KEPT INTACT in context/aiw-console/records/VEREDICTO-ROADMAP-TREE-V1.md, which already served its purpose — roadmap_tree_v1 is consumable and held up against real data without inventing; its limit is what it delegates to the contract (the status vocabulary and the objective/phase derivation rule), an input the emitter inherits. The prototype→shell gate that D-047 wrote dissolves here: the multi-console comes to depend on the identical port. This run will not be executed again; its completed status says that it ran and closed (the code exists and the verdict is written) and closeout_result says HOW it closed. There is no token 'descartado' (discarded) in the closed vocabulary of run (CONTRATO §11.a: planned/active/blocked/completed), so the retirement travels in closeout_result, which is a free string (§14), and in this note. The phase stays at the end of the objective: it is history, not plan.
